subject: rating-scale
detail: Shelfie's README and OpenAPI spec say ratings are 1-10 in a field called 'score'; Shelfie's code and Readr's code both use 1-5 'stars'. Documentation vs code, not code vs code (A-C03, A-C04).
solutions: 1-5 stars as both apps' code does
1-10 as Shelfie's old docs say (would need a conversion and a decision from the user)
recommended: 1-5 integer stars: what both apps actually do, and the user said to trust the code

subject: export-format
detail: Shelfie's README and spec promise CSV at /api/v1/books/export.csv; the code returns JSON at /api/books/export (A-C01, A-C02).
solutions: CSV as the docs claim (new work, not in any source's behaviour)
recommended: JSON only; CSV listed as a possible later addition if the user wants it

subject: rating-cardinality
detail: Both apps append a new ratings row each time a book is rated, so a book collects several ratings and Shelfie's export repeats it. A shared, multi-person app needs a clear rule.
solutions: One rating per person per book; rating again replaces it
Keep every rating as history and show the latest or the average
recommended: One rating per person per book (unique key, upsert); history is not in the user's request

subject: write-persistence
detail: Neither source ever commits a transaction, so (inferred from sqlite3 defaults; not run) writes would be lost when the process exits; neither enables SQLite foreign keys, so ratings and list entries can point at missing books.
solutions: Commit every write and turn on PRAGMA foreign_keys in the unified app
recommended: Commit every write, enable foreign keys, and test that data survives a restart

subject: existing-data-import
detail: Both apps key books with their own integer ids in separate SQLite files (shelfie.db, readr.db). Importing both into one database would collide on ids and require re-keying Readr's books and rewriting its ratings and list_books rows; there is also no user to own imported rows. No database files were provided and nothing shows whether real data exists.
solutions: Start the unified app with an empty database; import is out of scope for now
Write an import that re-keys Readr's ids into the unified Book table and assigns all rows to one chosen person (destructive-risk migration needing its own plan and approval)
recommended: Start empty; if the user has data worth keeping, plan the import separately with templates/migration-plan.md, a backup and a dry run

subject: path-version-prefix
detail: Shelfie's spec uses /api/v1/...; its code serves /api/... (A-C05). Readr has no API.
recommended: Use /api/... (the observed shape); versioning is not needed for a new single app
